institution: Dept. of Computer Science and Engineering University of California, San Diego La Jolla, CA In the world of big data, large but costly to label datasets dominate many fields. Active learning, a semi-supervised alternative to the standard PAC-learning model, was introduced to explore whether adaptive labeling could learn concepts with exponentially fewer labeled samples. While previous results show that active learning performs no better than its supervised alternative for important concept classes learning called Reliable and Probably Useful (RPU) learning. In this model, our In recent years, the availability of big data and the high cost of labeling has lead to a surge of interest in active learning, an adaptive, semi-supervised learning paradigm. In traditional active learning, learner receives unlabeled samples x from D with the ability to query an oracle for the labeling approximately learning the concept class with high probability (PAC-learning). Instead, active learning assumes unlabeled samples are inexpensive, and rather aims to minimize expensive queries to the oracle. While active learning requires exponentially fewer labeled samples than PAC-learning However, recent results point to the fact that with slight relaxations or additions to the paradigm, such concept classes can be learned with exponentially fewer queries.
